metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: Recall the pure-drift approximation for the variance (Equation 18.8) and the within-line covariance across generations (Equation 18.9) for the design of a single selected line. Here we present corresponding expressions for the selection plus control and divergence selection designs (assuming there are no genotype × environmental interactions between lines). For unidirectional selection plus a control population $$ \begin{aligned}R_{C}(t)=\overline{z}_{s,t}-\overline{z}_{c,t}&=\left(\mu+g_{s,t}+b_{t}+e_{s,t}\right)-\left(\mu+g_{c,t}+b_{t}+e_{c,t}\right)\\&=\left(g_{s,t}-g_{c,t}\right)+\left(e_{s,t}-e_{c,t}\right)\end{aligned} $$

Similarly, for divergent selection $$ R_{C}(t)=\overline{z}_{s u,t}-\overline{z}_{s d,t}=\left(g_{s u,t}-g_{s d,t}\right)+\left(e_{s u,t}-e_{s d,t}\right) $$ Because each term in Equations 18.28 and 18.29 is independent, applying Equations 18.4 and 18.5 yields a pure-drift approximation for the variance in response in generation t of $$ \sigma^{2}\left[R_{C}(t)\right]=\left(2f_{t}+B_{0}\right)h^{2}\sigma_{z}^{2}+B_{t}\sigma_{z}^{2}\simeq\left(t A+B_{0}\right)h^{2}\sigma_{z}^{2}+B_{t}\sigma_{z}^{2} $$ and the covariance between generations within the same line $$ \begin{aligned}\sigma\left[R_{C}(t),R_{C}(t^{\prime})\right]&=\left(2f_{t}+B_{0}\right)h^{2}\sigma_{z}^{2}\\&\simeq\left(t A+B_{0}\right)\sigma_{z}^{2}h^{2}\qquad\text{for}t<t^{\prime}\end{aligned} $$
